summary: Keiki Yabuki was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Tohoku High School, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Taisho University, Nihon University, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and the University of Tokyo.
Keikyo Nakamikado works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakamikado held research positions at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and the Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute (attested 2015).

Keinin Hayashi is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Hayashi served as a lecturer at Waseda University and held full-time research posts at the Eastern Institute (attested 1998) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned a PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham and studied at the University of the Highlands and Islands. Strickland held positions at the University of the Highlands and Islands and La Trobe University.

Keishin Okamura was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor and visiting professor at Koyasan University, and as a professor at Kochi University from around 1961 to 1995.

Keisho Tsukamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate at Tohoku University. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University, Professor Emeritus at Tohoku University, and President of Hosen Gakuen College.

Keith Dowman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He held an appointment at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He served as a lecturer and professor at Shuchiin University, and as a lecturer and research institute director at Taisho University.

Keizaburō Mizuno is a specialist in archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served at the Tokyo National Museum, as Professor Emeritus at Tokyo Fine Arts School, and directed the Niigata Prefectural and Hanzomon museums.

Ken McLeod works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia and studied with traditional teachers including Kalu Rinpoche. He served as resident teacher at Kagyu Droden Kunchab.
Kendall R. Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Mario Poceski and earned a PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.

Kengo Harimoto is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass. Harimoto has held posts at Mahidol University (attested 2020) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2022).

Kenichi Kuranishi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kuranishi has held an associate professorship at Taisho University (attested 2013–2026) and a research fellowship at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1973 to 1984. He held a post at Kokugakuin University around 1987.
Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1971 to 1980 under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from roughly 1973 to 1984 and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2019.

Kenji Shimada was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history who studied at Kyoto University from roughly 1938 to 1941. He later worked as a researcher at Kyoto University and its Institute for Research in Humanities from circa 1949 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University under doctoral supervisors including Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter C. Bisschop. Takahashi held a JSPS fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.
Kenji Watanabe is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jozef Deleu. He held an assistant post at Taisho University around 1978.
Kenjiu Kasawara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, with instruction under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
